paper_title: Exact solution for the collective non-Markovian decay of two fully excited quantum emitters (Lanuza, 2024, arXiv)
core_reasoning_1:
\section*{Claim}
Let
\[
\widehat N:=\sum_{j=1}^{2}\widehat a_j^\dagger \widehat a_j+\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}\widehat b_m^\dagger \widehat b_m
\]
and let the Hamiltonian be
\[
\widehat H/\hbar=\Delta\sum_{j=1}^{2}\widehat a_j^\dagger \widehat a_j
-J\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}\left(\widehat b_m^\dagger\widehat b_{m+1}+\widehat b_m\widehat b_{m+1}^\dagger\right)
+g\sum_{j=1}^{2}\left(\widehat a_j\widehat b_j^\dagger+\widehat a_j^\dagger\widehat b_j\right).
\]
Then \([\widehat N,\widehat H]=0\). Hence an initial state with exactly two excitations remains in the two-excitation subspace.

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad & \widehat N:=\widehat N_a+\widehat N_b,\quad
\widehat N_a:=\sum_{j=1}^{2}\widehat a_j^\dagger \widehat a_j,\quad
\widehat N_b:=\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}\widehat b_m^\dagger \widehat b_m,\\
\text{(P2)}\quad & \widehat H/\hbar:=\widehat H_a+\widehat H_b+\widehat H_{ab},\\
\text{(P3)}\quad & \widehat H_a:=\Delta\sum_{j=1}^{2}\widehat a_j^\dagger\widehat a_j,\\
\text{(P4)}\quad & \widehat H_b:=-J\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}\left(\widehat b_m^\dagger\widehat b_{m+1}+\widehat b_m\widehat b_{m+1}^\dagger\right),\\
\text{(P5)}\quad & \widehat H_{ab}:=g\sum_{j=1}^{2}\left(\widehat a_j\widehat b_j^\dagger+\widehat a_j^\dagger\widehat b_j\right),\\
\text{(P6)}\quad & [\widehat N_a,\widehat a_j]=-\widehat a_j,\quad [\widehat N_a,\widehat a_j^\dagger]=\widehat a_j^\dagger,\quad
[\widehat N_b,\widehat b_m]=-\widehat b_m,\quad [\widehat N_b,\widehat b_m^\dagger]=\widehat b_m^\dagger,\\
\text{(P7)}\quad & [\widehat N_a,\widehat b_m]=[\widehat N_a,\widehat b_m^\dagger]=[\widehat N_b,\widehat a_j]=[\widehat N_b,\widehat a_j^\dagger]=0,\\
\text{(P8)}\quad & [X,YZ]=[X,Y]Z+Y[X,Z],\\
\text{(P9)}\quad & [\widehat N,\widehat O]=0 \Longrightarrow \widehat O \text{ preserves eigenspaces of }\widehat N.
\end{align*}

\section*{Derivation}
\begin{align*}
[\widehat N,\widehat H_a]
&=\Delta\sum_{j=1}^{2}[\widehat N,\widehat a_j^\dagger\widehat a_j]
&&\text{by (P3) and linearity}\\
&=\Delta\sum_{j=1}^{2}\left([\widehat N,\widehat a_j^\dagger]\widehat a_j+\widehat a_j^\dagger[\widehat N,\widehat a_j]\right)
&&\text{by (P8)}\\
&=\Delta\sum_{j=1}^{2}\left(\widehat a_j^\dagger\widehat a_j-\widehat a_j^\dagger\widehat a_j\right)
&&\text{by (P6) and (P7)}\\
&=0.
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
[\widehat N,\widehat b_m^\dagger\widehat b_{m+1}]
&=[\widehat N,\widehat b_m^\dagger]\widehat b_{m+1}+\widehat b_m^\dagger[\widehat N,\widehat b_{m+1}]
&&\text{by (P8)}\\
&=\widehat b_m^\dagger\widehat b_{m+1}-\widehat b_m^\dagger\widehat b_{m+1}
&&\text{by (P6) and (P7)}\\
&=0,\\
[\widehat N,\widehat b_m\widehat b_{m+1}^\dagger]
&=[\widehat N,\widehat b_m]\widehat b_{m+1}^\dagger+\widehat b_m[\widehat N,\widehat b_{m+1}^\dagger]
&&\text{by (P8)}\\
&=-\widehat b_m\widehat b_{m+1}^\dagger+\widehat b_m\widehat b_{m+1}^\dagger
&&\text{by (P6) and (P7)}\\
&=0.
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
[\widehat N,\widehat H_b]
&=-J\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}\left([\widehat N,\widehat b_m^\dagger\widehat b_{m+1}]+[\widehat N,\widehat b_m\widehat b_{m+1}^\dagger]\right)
&&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=0
&&\text{using the two identities above.}
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
[\widehat N,\widehat a_j\widehat b_j^\dagger]
&=[\widehat N,\widehat a_j]\widehat b_j^\dagger+\widehat a_j[\widehat N,\widehat b_j^\dagger]
&&\text{by (P8)}\\
&=-\widehat a_j\widehat b_j^\dagger+\widehat a_j\widehat b_j^\dagger
&&\text{by (P6) and (P7)}\\
&=0,\\
[\widehat N,\widehat a_j^\dagger\widehat b_j]
&=[\widehat N,\widehat a_j^\dagger]\widehat b_j+\widehat a_j^\dagger[\widehat N,\widehat b_j]
&&\text{by (P8)}\\
&=\widehat a_j^\dagger\widehat b_j-\widehat a_j^\dagger\widehat b_j
&&\text{by (P6) and (P7)}\\
&=0.
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
[\widehat N,\widehat H_{ab}]
&=g\sum_{j=1}^{2}\left([\widehat N,\widehat a_j\widehat b_j^\dagger]+[\widehat N,\widehat a_j^\dagger\widehat b_j]\right)
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=0,\\
[\widehat N,\widehat H/\hbar]
&=[\widehat N,\widehat H_a]+[\widehat N,\widehat H_b]+[\widehat N,\widehat H_{ab}]
&&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=0.
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
[\widehat N,\widehat H]&=\hbar[\widehat N,\widehat H/\hbar]
&&\text{multiplication by }\hbar\\
&=0,\\
\widehat N\vert\psi(0)\rangle=2\vert\psi(0)\rangle
&\Longrightarrow \vert\psi(t)\rangle \text{ remains in the }N=2\text{ eigenspace}
&&\text{by (P9).}
\end{align*}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{[\widehat N,\widehat H]=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad N(t)=N(0)=2\text{ for the fully excited initial state}}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_4:
\section*{Claim}
Define
\[
C(\omega,z):=\sum_{j=-\infty}^{\infty}\widetilde C_{1,j}(\omega)z^{1-j},\qquad
C_\sigma(\omega,z):=\frac{1}{2}\left(C(\omega,z)+\sigma z^{-1}C(\omega,z^{-1})\right).
\]
Then, on the unit circle \(z=e^{iqd}\),
\[
C(\omega,e^{iqd})=e^{-iqd/2}\widetilde C_{1,q}(\omega),
\]
and the parity component satisfies the inversion identity
\[
C_\sigma(\omega,z^{-1})=\sigma z C_\sigma(\omega,z).
\]

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad & C(\omega,z):=\sum_{j=-\infty}^{\infty}\widetilde C_{1,j}(\omega)z^{1-j},\\
\text{(P2)}\quad & \widetilde C_{1,q}(\omega):=\sum_{j=-\infty}^{\infty}\widetilde C_{1,j}(\omega)e^{-iqd(j-3/2)},\\
\text{(P3)}\quad & z=e^{iqd}\Longrightarrow z^{1-j}=e^{iqd(1-j)},\\
\text{(P4)}\quad & e^{-iqd(j-3/2)}=e^{iqd(1-j)}e^{iqd/2},\\
\text{(P5)}\quad & C_\sigma(\omega,z):=\frac{1}{2}\left(C(\omega,z)+\sigma z^{-1}C(\omega,z^{-1})\right),\\
\text{(P6)}\quad & \sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\Longrightarrow \sigma^2=1,\quad z\ne0.
\end{align*}

\section*{Derivation}
\begin{align*}
C(\omega,e^{iqd})
&=\sum_{j=-\infty}^{\infty}\widetilde C_{1,j}(\omega)e^{iqd(1-j)}
&&\text{by (P1) and (P3)}\\
&=e^{-iqd/2}\sum_{j=-\infty}^{\infty}\widetilde C_{1,j}(\omega)e^{iqd(1-j)}e^{iqd/2}
&&\text{multiplication by }e^{-iqd/2}e^{iqd/2}=1\\
&=e^{-iqd/2}\sum_{j=-\infty}^{\infty}\widetilde C_{1,j}(\omega)e^{-iqd(j-3/2)}
&&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=e^{-iqd/2}\widetilde C_{1,q}(\omega)
&&\text{by (P2).}
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
C_\sigma(\omega,z^{-1})
&=\frac{1}{2}\left(C(\omega,z^{-1})+\sigma z C(\omega,z)\right)
&&\text{substitute }z^{-1}\text{ into (P5)}\\
\sigma z C_\sigma(\omega,z)
&=\frac{\sigma z}{2}\left(C(\omega,z)+\sigma z^{-1}C(\omega,z^{-1})\right)
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\sigma z C(\omega,z)+\sigma^2 C(\omega,z^{-1})\right)
&&\text{distribute }\sigma z\\
&=\frac{1}{2}\left(\sigma z C(\omega,z)+C(\omega,z^{-1})\right)
&&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=C_\sigma(\omega,z^{-1})
&&\text{comparison with the first line.}
\end{align*}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{C(\omega,e^{iqd})=e^{-iqd/2}\widetilde C_{1,q}(\omega),\qquad C_\sigma(\omega,z^{-1})=\sigma z C_\sigma(\omega,z)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_7:
\section*{Claim}
At fixed \(\omega\), if crossing the branch cut \(\zeta(S^1)\) adds \(\delta C_\sigma(z)\) and crossing the inverse branch cut adds \(\sigma z^{-1}\delta C_\sigma(z^{-1})\), then the double-jump increment is
\[
\delta^2 C_\sigma(z)=\delta C_\sigma(z)-\sigma z^{-1}\delta C_\sigma(z^{-1}),
\]
and the analytic-structure deconstruction can be written as
\[
C_\sigma(z)=\frac{1}{2}\delta^2C_\sigma(z)\left(\Phi(z)+\frac{1}{2}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\delta C_\sigma(z)+\frac{1}{2}r_\sigma(z).
\]

\section*{Premises}
\begin{align*}
\text{(P1)}\quad & C_\sigma^{(0)}(z):=C_\sigma(z),\\
\text{(P2)}\quad & C_\sigma^{(1)}(z)-C_\sigma^{(0)}(z):=\delta C_\sigma(z),\\
\text{(P3)}\quad & C_\sigma^{(2)}(z):=C_\sigma^{(0)}(z)-\delta C_\sigma(z)+\sigma z^{-1}\delta C_\sigma(z^{-1}),\\
\text{(P4)}\quad & \delta^2 C_\sigma(z):=C_\sigma^{(0)}(z)-C_\sigma^{(2)}(z),\\
\text{(P5)}\quad & r_\sigma(z):=2C_\sigma(z)+\delta C_\sigma(z)-\delta^2C_\sigma(z)\left(\Phi(z)+\frac{1}{2}\right),\\
\text{(P6)}\quad & z\ne0,\quad \sigma\in\{-1,+1\}.
\end{align*}

\section*{Derivation}
\begin{align*}
\delta^2 C_\sigma(z)
&:=C_\sigma^{(0)}(z)-C_\sigma^{(2)}(z)
&&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=C_\sigma^{(0)}(z)-\left(C_\sigma^{(0)}(z)-\delta C_\sigma(z)+\sigma z^{-1}\delta C_\sigma(z^{-1})\right)
&&\text{substitution from (P3)}\\
&=C_\sigma^{(0)}(z)-C_\sigma^{(0)}(z)+\delta C_\sigma(z)-\sigma z^{-1}\delta C_\sigma(z^{-1})
&&\text{distribute the minus sign}\\
&=\delta C_\sigma(z)-\sigma z^{-1}\delta C_\sigma(z^{-1})
&&\text{cancellation.}
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
r_\sigma(z)&:=2C_\sigma(z)+\delta C_\sigma(z)-\delta^2C_\sigma(z)\left(\Phi(z)+\frac{1}{2}\right)
&&\text{by (P5)}\\
2C_\sigma(z)&=r_\sigma(z)-\delta C_\sigma(z)+\delta^2C_\sigma(z)\left(\Phi(z)+\frac{1}{2}\right)
&&\text{solve for }2C_\sigma(z)\\
&=\delta^2C_\sigma(z)\left(\Phi(z)+\frac{1}{2}\right)-\delta C_\sigma(z)+r_\sigma(z)
&&\text{reordering terms}\\
C_\sigma(z)&=\frac{1}{2}\delta^2C_\sigma(z)\left(\Phi(z)+\frac{1}{2}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\delta C_\sigma(z)+\frac{1}{2}r_\sigma(z)
&&\text{division by }2.
\end{align*}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\delta^2 C_\sigma(z)=\delta C_\sigma(z)-\sigma z^{-1}\delta C_\sigma(z^{-1}),\qquad
C_\sigma(z)=\frac{1}{2}\delta^2C_\sigma(z)\left(\Phi(z)+\frac{1}{2}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\delta C_\sigma(z)+\frac{1}{2}r_\sigma(z)}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
